title: Quick Revision: Work and Energy

table: W = F × s (force × displacement in its direction)

bullets: Work is done only if a force moves the body. **No displacement means no work** (e.g. pushing a wall).
Work is **positive** when force and displacement are in the same direction, **negative** when opposite (e.g. friction), and **zero** when they are at right angles.
1 J of work is done when a force of 1 N moves a body 1 m in its direction.
**Law of conservation of energy:** energy can only change from one form to another; the total stays constant.
A freely falling body: PE changes into KE, and PE + KE stays the same at every point.
Doubling the speed makes KE **four times**, because KE depends on v^{2}.

box: Take g = 9.8 m/s^{2} unless the question says 10 m/s^{2}.
1 kW = 1000 W · 1 hour = 3600 s · Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h)

bullets: Using mass in grams. Convert to kg first.
Forgetting to square the velocity in ½mv^{2}.

blocks.p: 1. Find the potential energy of a 2 kg ball held 5 m above the ground (g = 10 m/s^{2}).
2. A 60 W bulb glows for 10 hours. How many units of energy does it use?
